newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's C.Bank to accept membership in BIS.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's C.Bank to accept membership in BIS.

text.p: The National Bank of Croatia (NBH) said on Friday it would accept an offer by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) to become a member along with most of the other former Yugoslav republics.
"BIS has asked central banks of Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Macedonia to join," NBH said.
"Membership was not offered to Yugoslavia's central bank, which has long blocked a solution of the re-distribution of the heritage of the former National Bank of (federal) Yugoslavia," it said.
The former NBY has $600 million in gold and cash and 8,000 shares with suspended voting rights with the Swiss-based BIS, NBH said.
The BIS executive council also offered the four banks to buy 10 shares each from a special emission by end May, so the BIS main board could decide on their admittance in June.

"Considering that the membership offer does not affect or condition the re-distribution talks and does recognize five new states in the territory of former Yugoslavia, Croatia's National Bank has deemed the offer acceptable," the bank said. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
